d.coyote_time: Grace period after walking off an edge during which a jump still works. It makes jumps between platforms feel fair; 0 disables it.
d.jump_buffer: A jump pressed shortly before landing is remembered and fires on touchdown. Higher is more forgiving; 0 requires exact timing.
d.slide_accel: On surfaces steeper than the maximum slope you slide down: this is how fast the slide picks up speed. 0 = you stop on the slope.
d.floor_snap_distance: Walking down steps or slopes, you stay glued to the floor if it is within this distance, instead of flying for an instant. Too high pulls you down edges.
d.collision_quality: Number of probes testing the body against walls and floors. 1 is fastest but can miss thin edges; 3 is the most reliable on stairs and corners.
d.obj_lin_damping: Share of speed an object loses every second, regardless of contacts. Higher = objects stop sooner, as if moving through something thick.
d.obj_ang_damping: Like linear damping, but for rotation: higher values stop spinning objects sooner.
d.obj_air_drag: Air resistance, growing with the square of speed: barely noticeable when slow, it shortens long, fast throws.
d.obj_sleep_lin: Below this speed an object counts as still. Still objects stop being simulated and cost nothing.
d.obj_sleep_ang: Below this rotation speed an object counts as not turning (see the speed threshold).
d.obj_sleep_time: How long an object must stay below both thresholds before it goes to sleep. Too short can freeze objects mid-wobble; too long keeps them jittering.
d.obj_fill_ratio: For objects that are not closed solids, mass comes from the bounding-box volume times this factor, because the box overestimates the real volume.
d.impulse_ref_mass: Kick and throw forces refer to an object of this mass. A heavier object gets proportionally less speed, a lighter one more.
d.grab_spring: How quickly a held object catches up with its place in front of you. Low = floaty and delayed; high = rigid and immediate.
d.grab_pull_time: Right after grabbing, the object is pulled towards you through everything for this time, so it does not get stuck behind other things.
d.grab_out_time: Then it moves out to the holding distance, still ignoring collisions, in this time. With both at 0 the object is taken where it is.
d.tick_rate: How many times per second movement and physics are updated. Higher is smoother but uses more CPU; lower it on slow computers or heavy models.
help.title: What is DagaWASD?
help.intro: An extension for exploring your SketchUp model in first person, like a video game, with real physics for objects.
help.1: Start with the ▶ button, the toolbar or [Ctrl]+[PgUp]. [ESC] exits at any time.
help.2: Move with [W][A][S][D] and the mouse: [Space] jumps, [C] crouches, [Shift] runs. Stairs and slopes are climbed automatically.
help.3: Groups and components become physical as soon as you touch them: they fall, bounce and tip over. Mass, friction and bounce come from the material name (wood, metal, glass…).
help.4: [Alt] shows info on the object in the crosshair, [K] kicks it, [G] grabs and throws it: hold the key to charge.
help.5: Objects moved by the physics can be put back with [Ctrl]+[Z] after exiting.
help.6: Changes made here apply immediately. The switch at the top shows basic, advanced or expert settings; the search box finds a setting by name.
lvl.h2: Also fine-tuning of movement, camera and physics
lvl.h3: Every setting, including the simulation's internal parameters
h.grab_pull_time: Time the object takes to come to you, passing through everything
h.grab_out_time: Time to reach the holding distance; then collisions resume (0 + 0 = no pull)
rt.grab_lost: slipped from your hands: something is in the way
mt.note: The physical material is found from the first recognised word in: the material painted on the group, the material covering most of its faces, the group's name, the definition's name. Keywords are comma-separated and match anywhere in the name; built-in material names are recognised in every language.
mt.name: Material
rt.grab_loose: not a group or component: group the geometry to grab it
keys.grab_inner: Grab the innermost object, taking it out of its group
h.charge_bar: Shows throw and kick power under the crosshair
h.throw_charge_time: Spin only in the last 10% of the charge
keys.zoom: Wheel: zoom · middle button: reset · holding an object: move it closer or farther
rt.kick_charge: charging the kick — release K to kick
h.accel_time: Seconds to reach full speed. Lower = snappier start
h.jump_cut_factor: Releasing Space while rising shortens the jump. 1 = always full height
h.coyote_time: You can still jump for a moment after leaving the ledge
h.jump_buffer: A jump pressed shortly before landing is remembered
h.crouch_transition: How quickly you crouch and stand up
h.step_height: Steps up to this height are climbed while walking (stairs)
h.max_slope_deg: Steeper than this and you slide instead of climbing
h.slide_accel: How fast you pick up speed sliding down a steep slope
h.collision_quality: 1 = fast (one probe) · 3 = accurate (reliable ledges and stairs)
h.pad_look: 4 and 6 turn, 8 and 2 look up and down, also together: for when there is no mouse
h.pad_look_speed: Degrees per second at full speed with 4 and 6
h.pad_look_speed_v: Degrees per second at full speed with 8 and 2
h.pad_look_accel: Seconds to reach full speed: a short tap moves a little, for aiming. 0 = at once
h.gamepad_enabled: Xbox or compatible controller (XInput). Left stick walks, right stick looks; A jumps, B crouches, X uses, Y grabs, right trigger kicks, left trigger runs; D-pad up/down zooms, View frees the mouse, Menu exits
h.gamepad_look_speed: Turning speed with the right stick fully tilted
h.gamepad_deadzone: Part of the stick travel that is ignored: raise it if the view drifts on its own
h.gamepad_curve: Above 1 the right stick is slower near the centre, for fine aiming
h.gamepad_rumble: The gamepad vibrates on hard landings
h.cam_roll: The camera banks slightly when moving sideways
h.head_bob_freq: Scales with actual speed: running makes the stride quicker
h.land_dip: Springy camera dip when touching down after a jump
h.obj_walls: Objects bounce off walls and vertical surfaces
h.obj_tipping: An object tips over once its centre of mass leaves the support polygon
h.obj_bounce: Used only when the material is not recognised
h.obj_air_drag: Grows with the square of speed: slows down long throws
h.obj_sleep_time: A body falls asleep only after staying still for this long
h.obj_use_materials: Density, friction and bounciness taken from the material name (wood, stone, metal, glass, rubber, ball, cardboard, plastic)
h.obj_density: For objects with no recognised material
h.obj_fill_ratio: Only for objects that are not closed solids (their bounding box overestimates the volume)
h.player_mass: Sets the mass ratios used in impacts
h.push_enabled: Walking into a light object moves it
h.knockback_enabled: A moving object that hits the player pushes them
h.use_range: Shows the object's name, distance, mass and material
h.kick_force: Speed given to an object of the reference mass at full charge
h.impulse_ref_mass: A heavier object starts off proportionally slower
h.grab_spring: Lower = the object trails the hand with more inertia
h.tick_rate: Applied immediately, even while the simulation is running

h.hud_cross_outline: Keeps it visible on light surfaces
h.hud_bar_zone_color: Final stretch of the throw charge
h.respawn_enabled: Falling into the void takes you back to where you were just before
h.respawn_fall_time: Seconds of free fall before going back
d.respawn_fall_time: Only real falling counts, not the rise of a jump. You go back to where you were half a second before leaving the ground, away from the edge.
f.respawn_exit_count: Exit after respawns in a row
h.respawn_exit_count: How many respawns after a fall in a row exit the mode
d.respawn_exit_count: If the respawn spot makes you fall again, the mode closes instead of falling forever. 0 = never.
h.respawn_calm_time: Seconds on the ground without a break that reset the respawn count

keys.record: Record a path: press to start, again to stop
h.path_smooth: Seconds over which movement is averaged: removes head bob and mouse jerks. 0 = exactly as recorded
h.path_speed: Speed of playback, scenes and video compared with the recorded walk
h.path_scene_step: Seconds of path between one scene and the next: less = more scenes, more faithful movement
h.path_video_size: Size of the images exported for the video
h.path_video_fps: Video frames per second: 25 or 30 for a normal video, 60 for smoother
path.note: In FPS mode press R to record what you see while walking, and R again to stop: the path is saved in the model. From here you can replay it, turn it into SketchUp scenes or into images for a video (the images do not include the sun, clouds and rain of the animated weather).

path.scenes.h: Create a scene every few seconds: playing the scenes or File › Export › Animation repeats the path
path.frames.h: Export the path as an AVI video or as PNG images (choose below, under Video)

h.bridge_enabled: Claude Code can draw in and query the open model
d.bridge_enabled: Opens a server on this computer only (127.0.0.1) that runs the Ruby code sent by Claude Code. Each request is a single operation: Ctrl+Z undoes it. Keep it off when you don't need it.
bridge.note: The bridge lets Claude Code draw directly in the open model and look at it. It only accepts requests from this computer, with a secret code that changes at every start (saved in %APPDATA%\DagaWASD\bridge.json). Anyone who can run programs as your user can use it: turn it on only when needed. It is never imported from a settings file.
bridge.fail: Cannot start: no free port between 47810 and 47819
f.bridge_live: Show the build step by step
h.bridge_live: Watch each solid appear in the view while Claude draws
d.bridge_live: Claude marks the end of each piece: at that point SketchUp redraws the view and waits for the chosen pause before continuing. It stays a single operation: Ctrl+Z removes everything. When off, the drawing arrives all at once at full speed.
h.bridge_step_delay: Longer = a slower build that is easier to follow
h.bridge_detail: How finely to watch each piece take shape
h.bridge_orbit: The camera slowly circles around what Claude is building
d.bridge_orbit: During step-by-step building the camera circles the new pieces and follows their size as they grow. It stops when the build ends.
sky.note: Sun, moon and stars cross the sky according to the date, the time and the model's location (Window › Model Info › Geo-location), in every view, not only while walking. When the sky is turned off, and before every save, the model gets its own shadow and sky settings back.
h.sky_enabled: Sun, moon, stars and sky colours follow the date and time
h.sky_now: Follows the computer clock, in the model's time zone
h.sky_hour: Local time at the model's location (e.g. 17:30)
h.sky_flow: Off: the sky stays still at the time above
h.sky_day_minutes: Real minutes for a whole day and night
h.sky_shadows: Turns on the model's shadows, which follow the sun
h.sky_colors: Dawn, sunset and night colour the sky and darken the scene
h.sky_body_size: Times their real size, which would look tiny
h.sky_star_count: Besides the brightest ones, which are always there
h.sky_fps: Per second while time passes: fewer = lighter on big models
h.sky_shadow_fps: Shadow recalculations per second while time passes: the heaviest part, fewer = smoother on big models
sky.old: before SketchUp 2023 the sky only shows while walking
h.sky_place_custom: Off: the model's location (Model Info › Geo-location)
h.sky_tz: Hours from UTC, without daylight saving
precip.note: Rain and snow fall around the camera in every view, not only while walking, and stop under roofs and trees. With the animated sky on they also cover the sky: grey, veiled sun, faint shadows. The model's own fog comes back when they are turned off and before every save.
h.precip_kind: Around the camera, in every view
h.precip_intensity: From a few drops to a downpour
h.precip_wind: Slants the rain and drives the snow
h.precip_wind_dir: Where it blows from: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west
h.precip_fog: Thicker the harder it falls, and with snow
h.precip_roofs: No rain under roofs, porches and trees
h.precip_radius: Larger = rain also in the distance, but sparser
h.precip_max: At full intensity: more = denser, heavier for the computer
h.precip_fps: Per second: fewer = lighter on big models
cloud.note: Clouds drift with the wind in every view and take the colour of the light: white by day, pink at sunset, dark at night, grey with rain. With the animated sky on, a cloud in front of the sun dims the light and the shadows; with rain or snow the sky closes up.
h.cloud_enabled: Cumulus clouds drifting across the sky
h.cloud_cover: How much of the sky they cover
h.cloud_shade: A cloud in front of the sun dims the light and the shadows
h.cloud_wind_dir: Where it blows from: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west
h.cloud_fps: Per second: fewer = lighter on big models
h.storm: Lightning while it rains or snows
h.snow_cover: Roofs, ground and treetops turn white while it snows, then melt
h.snow_cover_time: Real minutes to a full cover at maximum intensity
h.cloud_timelapse: When the sky's time runs faster, clouds race too (up to 30×)
presets.note: One click sets sky, time, rain, snow and clouds together. Sunrise and sunset are computed for the date and the place chosen in Date & time of day.
wp.dawn.h: The sun just risen, pink clouds
wp.sunset.h: Low sun, warm light, scattered clouds
wp.starry.h: The darkest hour, no clouds: moon and stars
wp.snownight.h: Steady snow that settles, overcast sky
wp.storm.h: Heavy rain, wind, lightning and thunder
